competition.flat_book_pnl: A flat seat has zero net financing/competition P&L: paper NAV earning SOFR is benchmarked at SOFR, so those flows cancel, and shocked-risk financing is zero.
competition.funding_basis: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 is the zero-return competition benchmark, not free alpha. Every seat has $100m paper NAV that may be described as earning SOFR, but that capital is equally funded/benchmarked at SOFR so those flows cancel. Deployed shocked-risk capital pays the same official SOFR on trusted standard-shock risk capital: the absolute MTM loss from a 1% adverse spot move, a 100bp (1 percentage point) adverse outright rate move, or a 100bp adverse curve/RV spread move. Supported STIR contracts use exchange DV01 and currency conversion; historical rows without that stamp keep the legacy duration-one vintage and are not silently restated. Equal risk capital receives equal financing treatment across asset classes. Notional is descriptive, not the funding base. A completely flat book — including no-trade-skeptic — therefore has zero net financing/competition P&L from SOFR cash or funding economics. Positive financing/carry alpha requires an explicit markable strategy that earns above SOFR or funds below SOFR. Weekends and holidays carry the last applicable published fixing until the next fixing. If official fixing history cannot be established, new funding accrual fails closed and prior canonical balances are preserved.
competition.instruction: Do not optimize for gross notional or fill available capacity. Size risk from plausible adverse paths and historical excursions while staying inside the trusted risk-capital and drawdown limits. Flat cash at SOFR is the zero benchmark, not a source of alpha. The no-trade-skeptic must include a structured funding_view on every new risk or NO_TRADE thesis: the frozen official SOFR fixing, the relevant SR3 forward-curve view, its own assessment of whether realized funding will print higher, lower, or about the same as the curve, and the implication for remaining at the zero SOFR benchmark versus paying SOFR on shocked-risk capital.
competition.objective: Finish with the highest cumulative net paper P&L across the 14 standing seats.

research_supplement.summary: Overnight, US Treasury yields moved lower with the 10-year at 4.84% and the 2-year at 4.46% as traders positioned for the jobs release; SOFR is 3.94% and futures imply a gradual rise toward the mid-4.3% area by late 2027. Equities stayed firm with the S&P 500 at 7688.62 and Nasdaq at 24315, while gold held 4113.5 after the US congressional shift initially pressured the dollar and lifted bullion. The Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4.0%, its first increase since the Iran war began, and warned inflation could approach 5%. Canada and the Bank of Canada renewed their inflation-targeting framework. Stress around AI-related leverage intensified, with SoftBank credit risk at a four-year high and banks reportedly marketing data-center loans. The period ahead turns on US employment data, ECB inputs toward the December meeting, and whether tech-financing strains broaden.

value-guy.invalidation: Cover the short if Australian-kiwi extends above 1.2453 while WTI returns toward 102, or if the cross is still at or above 1.2453 after thirty days.

causal.assumptions_right: The valuation assumption was right because the cross fell about one figure from 0.99 to 0.98 and has slipped further to 0.9777 without a new five-year high.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The risk frame underweighted the path that actually printed, in which oil fell from the 102.78 reference to 90.52 and the cross still declined, and it spent the invalidation on a March CORRA slide toward 2.24 that never started.
causal.causal_divergence: The convergence arrived with weaker oil, so the decline in AUDCAD cannot be credited to the strong-oil Canadian dollar sponsor that the original invalidation was written around.
causal.future_implication: A leftover AUDCAD z-score of 1.91 is not an automatic re-short, because oil at 90.52 no longer sponsors Canadian dollar strength the way a 102.78 tape did, and the live five-year extreme is now AUDNZD.
causal.observed_reality: The short was closed on 2026-11-05 near 0.98 after about seven days. The cross is 0.9777 today with a five-year z-score of 1.91, WTI is 90.52, CORRA cash is 2.52, and March CORRA is 2.885.
causal.original_belief: AUDCAD was historically rich at the 0.99 entry, so a short was expected to converge unless the cross printed a new five-year extreme while WTI stayed near 102.78, or unless March CORRA fell toward 2.24 with oil unchanged.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: Holding the short through 0.98 on the entry information alone would have improved the exit by only a small residual at today's 0.9777 mark, while leaving the book short the Canadian dollar after the oil justification had already started to fail.

postmortems.expression_assessment: Spot AUDCAD was the correct instrument for that peer gap, and the rate market did not need to be involved for the convergence to pay.
postmortems.future_rule: Do not reopen a covered value short unless the fundamental sponsor named at entry is still present, or a separate historical extreme with its own anchor has replaced it.
postmortems.lesson: When a valuation short converges while its commodity sponsor fades, the profit belongs to the original thesis, but the residual percentile is a new question and does not inherit the old ticket.
postmortems.thesis_assessment: The richness thesis was confirmed by the move from 0.99 through 0.98 to 0.9777, and it was confirmed while oil moved against the Canadian dollar.
postmortems.timing_assessment: Closing after about seven days at 0.98 banked the tactical gain with only a small residual to 0.9777, so the exit was acceptable even though the percentile has not fully normalized.
postmortems.what_failed: The written invalidation never identified an oil drop as the event that would retire the fundamental case, so a still-high percentile had no rule separating a finished ticket from a new one.
postmortems.what_worked: The short captured a real valuation convergence of about one figure inside a week, and the cover did not wait for an invalidation that never printed.

deployment_hurdle.benchmark: Official NY Fed SOFR 3.94 percent, effective 2026-11-04, ACT/360, charged on shocked risk capital. Flat cash at 3.94 is the zero benchmark.

candidate_assessments.rationale: Marked at 1.2453 versus a 1.2456 short entry. The five-year extreme is intact. One percent adverse on 10 million is about 100 thousand dollars, and 3.94 percent on that stub is too small to exit. The unchanged extreme does not earn a larger notional.
Implied 4.115 versus 3.94 cash is a 17.5 basis point market gap, not an expected gain above funding on shock capital. A short that needs the implied yield higher is exposed to a soft jobs print.
Implied 4.24 is 30 basis points over 3.94 cash. A receive or a pay has no priced edge beyond the contract itself, and shock capital into the jobs report is not covered by the funding hurdle.

deployment_hurdle.chosen_action_rationale: The Australian-kiwi short clears because a still-extreme cross outweighs a small funding charge on a 100 thousand dollar one-percent shock, so the existing 10 million is kept and not increased. December 2026 at 4.115 and March 2027 at 4.24 are markable and do not clear ahead of the jobs report.
